display_name: Sher Shah Suri & Rao Maldeo Rathore (Sammel, 1544)
one_line: Afghan emperor Sher Shah Suri and Rajput ruler Rao Maldeo Rathore during the tense Marwar campaign and Battle of Sammel in 1544 CE.

appearance.age_look: Sher Shah looks like a lean, battle-hardened man in his late 50s; Rao Maldeo looks like a tall, athletic man in his early 40s.
appearance.face: Sher Shah has a long oval face, wheatish-brown complexion, sharp nose, trimmed grey beard and calm, calculating eyes with a serious, focused expression; Rao Maldeo has a square jaw, slightly darker sun-browned skin, straight nose, neatly trimmed moustache and intense, proud eyes with a firm, resolute expression.
appearance.hair: Sher Shah’s hair is mostly hidden under a simple dark green flat turban with a wrapped tail, only a bit of short grey hair visible at the temples; Rao Maldeo has thick black hair parted in the middle, reaching just below the ears and tucked behind, covered partially by a saffron-raised Rajput-style turban with a folded tail and a small, plain metal boss at the front.
appearance.costume: Sher Shah wears a long, straight Afghan-style quilted coat (qabā) in muted earthy brown reaching below the knees, with a round neckline, simple toggles, and faint vertical stitched lines, over a pale off-white cotton tunic and loose off-white trousers; a dark maroon woollen waist sash is tied firmly with one end hanging, and a plain dark leather belt supports a scabbard; his feet are in sturdy brown leather shoes with rounded toes; Rao Maldeo wears a fitted long-sleeved angarkha-style tunic in deep indigo blue reaching to mid-thigh with side tie knots and a subtle diagonal overlap, over a saffron-yellow cotton kamarband sash tightly wrapped at the waist, and cream-coloured churidar-style fitted trousers with gathered folds at the ankles; over the tunic he has a sleeveless, riveted steel breastplate shaped to the torso, worn over a visible padded red cotton lining at the shoulders, and his feet are in simple tan leather mojari with slight upturned toes; both are fully and modestly covered.
appearance.signature: Sher Shah carries at his left side a slightly curved Indo-Afghan sword in a plain dark brown leather scabbard with simple brass fittings, right hand often resting on the hilt; Rao Maldeo carries a long Rajput talwar with a disc-pommel and cross-guard, in a polished dark leather scabbard with brass chape, and a round steel dhal shield strapped on his left forearm.

ref_desc: Sher Shah Suri is a lean, grey-bearded Afghan in a dark green turban, brown quilted coat, maroon sash and curved sword, while Rao Maldeo Rathore is a tall Rajput in a saffron turban, indigo angarkha, steel breastplate, saffron sash, talwar and shield.
sheet_prompt: Draw two full-body anime-style historical characters standing side by side: Sher Shah Suri and Rao Maldeo Rathore at Sammel, 1544 CE. Sher Shah is a lean, late-50s Afghan emperor with a long oval face, wheatish-brown skin, sharp nose and trimmed grey beard, his expression calm and calculating. His short grey hair is mostly hidden under a simple dark green flat turban with a wrapped tail. He wears a modest, era-accurate Afghan-style quilted coat in muted earthy brown reaching below the knees, with round neckline, faint vertical stitched lines and simple toggles, over a pale off-white tunic and loose off-white trousers. A dark maroon wool waist sash is tied firmly with one end hanging, and a plain dark leather belt supports a slightly curved Indo-Afghan sword in a dark brown leather scabbard with brass fittings at his left side; his right hand lightly rests on the hilt. His shoes are sturdy brown leather with rounded toes. Beside him, Rao Maldeo Rathore is a tall, early-40s Rajput ruler with a square jaw, sun-browned slightly darker complexion, straight nose, neatly trimmed moustache and intense, proud eyes, looking firm and resolute. His thick black hair, parted in the middle and reaching just below the ears, is tucked behind and partially covered by a saffron-raised Rajput-style turban with a folded tail and a small plain metal boss at the front. He wears a fitted long-sleeved indigo blue angarkha-style tunic to mid-thigh with diagonal overlap and side ties, tightly wrapped saffron-yellow cotton kamarband sash at the waist, and cream churidar trousers with gathered folds at the ankles. Over the tunic he has a sleeveless, historically plausible riveted steel breastplate with visible red padded cotton lining around the shoulders. His footwear is tan leather mojari with slightly upturned toes. At his left hip hangs a long Rajput talwar with disc-pommel and cross-guard in a polished dark leather scabbard with brass chape, and a round steel dhal shield is strapped on his left forearm. Keep both figures fully and modestly clothed, and emphasize the earthy brown, dark green, maroon, deep indigo blue and saffron yellow palette in a clean, clear model-sheet style front-facing pose that shows face, hair, headgear, armour, garments and weapons distinctly.
